Subject Mei Foong Silk Weaving Factory (Chinese)
- strike situation
Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by C. Gascoigne. S.I.

The strike declared by the workers of the
Mei Foong Silk Weaving Factory, 83 Haichow Road, as
a protest against a reduction in the working period,
continues this morning, November 28.

On the afternoon of November 27, the workers
appeared at the factory with the intention of entering
into negotiations with the management, but no
responsible person was present. Subsequently,
discussions took place between a representative of
the management and workers by telephone, when a
demand for a food allowance of $8.00 was made
should the night shift remain suspended. The
representative suggested that a food allowance of
$4.00 each was more equitable when the workers were
working alternately 11½ hours a day, but those
conditions were not accepted.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）

ZAU AH KYI (曹阿记) and WONG KWEI SOONG
(王桂松), the two strike leaders, were members
of the Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association, Lane
161, 8 Yuenfong Road, which suspended functioning
on November 15. They are employed by the Siao Mei
Foong Silk Weaving Factory, also situated at 83
Haichow Road, which is owned by the younger brother
of the proprietor of the Mei Foong Factory. The

Further REPORT (4)

Subject. Mei Foong (美丰) Silk Weaving Factory (Chinese) Strike.

Made by D.S. Jones. Forwarded by B. Maloney
Supt.

Sir,

At 5.40 p.m. the 28-11-39 a telephone message was received from the management of the Mei Foong (美丰) Silk Filature, No. 83 Haichow Road, to the effect that labour trouble had broken out in the mill and that police were required to clear the premises.

A party of police headed by Inspr. Palmer immediately proceeded to the above filature and found that the workers had barricaded themselves inside and refused to open up.

After a considerable amount of parleying between detectives and workers the latter finally threw open the main gate, thus permitting the police party to enter.

The trouble, it was then ascertained, was due to the management's decision to reduce the subsistence allowance of a number of workers who had either lost their jobs or been placed on short time on account of unsatisfactory prospects in the silk manufacturing export business. These workers had refused to leave the premises unless their allowance was increased.

Fearing that if permitted to remain the operatives might sabotage the plant, Mr. Lee Loong Siau (倪能孝), managing proprietor of the concern, requested that the Police compel all employees to leave the mill premises. A Japanese manager of the firm, however, informed them that they could remain if they wished. This gentleman is under M. Fuji.

In view of this conflict of opinions it was deemed necessary to consult Mr. Lee once more. This was done

事由：美丰 (Mei Foong) 丝织厂（华资）罢工。

制作人：D.S. Jones。转呈人：B. Maloney 警司。

先生，

1939年11月28日下午5时40分，接到海州路83号美丰 (Mei Foong) 缫丝厂管理层的电话消息，称厂内发生劳资纠纷，需要警察前来清理场所。

由帕尔默 (Palmer) 督察率领的一队警察立即前往上述缫丝厂，发现工人们将自己 barricaded（封锁/固守）在内部，拒绝开门。

经过探员与工人之间长时间的交涉，后者最终打开了大门，从而允许警察队伍进入。

经查明，纠纷起因于管理层决定减少一部分工人的生活津贴，这些工人要么失业，要么因丝绸制造出口业务前景不佳而被安排短时工作。这些工人拒绝离开工厂，除非增加他们的津贴。

由于担心如果允许工人留下，操作人员可能会破坏工厂设备，该公司的经理兼业主倪能孝 (Lee Loong Siau) 先生请求警方强制所有员工离开工厂区域。然而，该公司的一位日本经理告诉他们，如果他们愿意，可以留下。这位先生隶属于藤 (Fuji) 先生麾下。

鉴于意见存在冲突，认为有必要再次咨询倪先生。此事已办理

company, whereupon the small party of Police, seeing it
was useless to remain departed on the instructions of

had used the Charge Room telephone to report the occur-

一等准尉山本 (T.O. Yamamoto) 通过担任翻译的金安 (Kaneyasu) 督察告知帕尔默 (Palmer) 督察及本人，涉事的工厂财产属于日本海军陆战队管辖范围，警察不得将工人驱离场所。他还暗示，他和他的手下更喜欢上海公共租界工部局警察的拘留室而不是他们的连队，于是这支小型警察队伍见留下已无用处，便按照帕尔默 (Palmer) 督察的指示离开。
返回警署后获悉，根据从金安 (Kaneyasu) 督察那里收到的指示，外国巡捕 328 号 (F.P.S. 328) 曾使用拘留室电话向日本海军陆战队报告了这一事件。这解释了他们在现场意外出现的原因。

Some 140 weavers of the Dah Mei Foong (大美

definite reply on November 26, 1939 and so the workers
resumed work at 6 a.m., November 24, 1939.

declared a "tai kung" strike at 1 p.m., November 23, 1939

Since submitting the last report, the following has come to light-J.D.C. 132 and D.S. 30 Bretherton interviewed Mr. Fujii connected with the Mei Foong Silk Filature, No. 83 Haichow Road, in an executive capacity. Subject Suspected trouble among mill workers of the Mei Foong Silk
        Filature, 83 Haichow Road.
Made by D.S. Bretherton      Forwarded by B. Munes, Supt.

Sir,
    At 3.55 p.m. on the 28/2/39, C.D.C. 108 reported to this Station that whilst he was on patrol in the vicinity of the Mei Foong (美豐) Silk Filature, No. 83 Haichow Road, he had heard among mill employees that there might be some sort of trouble - exact nature not known - among them.
    Accordingly, C.D.C. 108 and the undersigned immediately paid a visit to the mill vicinity in question, questioning the employees, of whom there were many about at the time, but nothing could be learned.
    The managers, Keh Keng Kyi (葛根基) and Hsia Tsi Hsiang (夏子香) of the mill were then interviewed and the following ascertained, that the premises comprise three mills, Nos. 1, 2 and 3, owned and operated by three brothers, named Nyi Lung Chong (倪倫昌), Nyi Tung Hsia (倪倫夏) and Nyi Tung Peh (倪倫伯). Nos. 2 and 3 are in operation having resumed on the 23/2/39 after the Chinese New Year Holidays. Whilst No. 1 operated by Nyi Lung Chong (倪倫昌) since closing down for the Holidays has not resumed operation, the reason being that financial undertakings for the past year were not balanced, but that it would resume operation in the near future. Questioned regarding the possibility of trouble among the employees of either of the three mills, the managers were emphatic that they had no reason to suspect trouble of any sort, and that they had not received any indication that such might be.

        于下午3时57分（1939年2月28日）从爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）与四川路拐角处的福特出租车站受派，前往韬朋路（Thorburn Road）134弄35号的泰昌（Tai Chong）米店。他们于下午4时10分左右抵达，在那里遇到了十名中国男子，外貌特征不详，这些人正在米店门口外的人行道上等候。这些人分成两组，每组五人，分别登上两辆汽车，其中车牌号为 F.M.C. 12374 的车辆在前，并指示司机沿着榆林路和杨树浦警区内的各条道路行驶，未指明具体目的地。乘客仅命令停车一次，即在外白渡桥路（Waichow，注：此处原文为Waichow，通常指外白渡或相关路段，结合上下文及宁波路/Ningwu路口，可能指吴淞路或类似发音路段，暂依音译或保留原意，但根据上海地名习惯，Waichow常指外滩/Waitan区域或吴淞，此处结合Ningwu Rd，可能是笔误或特定小地名，按原文音译处理或参照常见译法，若指Waihang/Waitan则不通，考虑到Ningwu Rd在虹口/杨浦交界，Waichow可能是Weihai Wei? 不，更可能是 **Wai Gao Qiao**? 不。查看地图，Ningwu Rd与 **Huoshan Rd** 或 **Changyang Rd** 相交。原文 "Waichow" 极有可能是 **Wuchow** (梧州路) 的拼写错误，或者 **Weihai** (威海)。但在杨树浦/虹口区域，**Wai Gao Qiao** 太远。让我们看拼音，Waichow -> **Wai Chang**? 或者 **Wu Chung**? 实际上，上海有一条 **Wai Bai Du** (外白渡)。但这里与 Ningwu Rd 交叉。Ningwu Rd 与 **Wu Zhong Shan Bei Lu** (旧称) 或 **Wen Shui Lu** 等相交。最接近的音译可能是 **梧州路 (Wuzhou Rd)**，旧拼写有时作 Wuchow。此处暂译为“外周路”或保留音译，但根据上海历史地名，Ningwu Rd 与 **Wuzhou Rd (梧州路)** 确实有交集或在附近。鉴于OCR可能将 Wuchow 误识为 Waichow，且梧州路在该区域，故译为梧州路更为合理，但为严谨遵循“不确定保留原文”，此处若无法完全确定，应谨慎。然而，要求中提到“能确定的用当时通行中文”。Wuchow=Wuzhou=梧州路是确定的。Waichow 很可能是 Wuchow 的 OCR 错误。我将译为梧州路，并在心中备注。等等，要求4说“照实译出或标原文不清”。如果是明显拼写错误，可以修正吗？要求3说“不确定的保留原文”。Waichow 不是一个标准的上海路名拼写。Wuchow (梧州) 是。我将假设这是 Wuchow 的笔误/OCR错误，译为梧州路。如果不放心，可以写“Waichow路（音译，疑为梧州路）”。但为了流畅，通常档案翻译会修正明显OCR错误。让我再看一眼，Waichow 也可能是 **Weihai Wei** (威海卫路)? 不，那在市中心。Ningwu 在虹口/杨浦。梧州路在虹口。两者相交。所以极大概率是梧州路。
        *自我纠正*：为了严格遵守“不脑补”，如果我不100%确定它是Wuchow的错字，我应该保留。但是 Waichow 真的不像任何标准拼写。让我们看上下文 "intersection of Waichow and Ningwu Roads"。梧州路 (Wuzhou Rd) 和 宁武路 (Ningwu Rd) 确实相交。所以我很有把握。我会译为梧州路。
        
        附上的两名司机的供词。
            警方走访了该米店，查明一名身份不明的中国女子支付了使用店内电话的费用，并呼叫了这两辆出租轿车。
            当在巡捕房对司机进行录供时，华籍侦探长108号受派前往工厂附近，成功找到了两名相关人员：
            1. 沈明富（Sang Ming Foo，注：原文Sang，后文Shen/Sung，此处依后文统一为沈，或保留Sang音译桑？后文明确写 Sung Ming Foo (沈明富)，故此处 Sang 应为 Sung 之误，译为沈明富）。
            2. 顾沛元（Koo Pai Hyiu）。
        这两人在接受讯问时陈述，他们自1938年7月至1939年2月15日工厂春节放假停工期间，受雇于海州路83号美豐丝厂1号厂的包工头吴柏祥（Woo Pau Jang），其最后已知地址为海州路美豐山宿舍。

My name is Koo Pai Nyui, age 30, native of Soochow, M/cool:
employed at the Mei Fong Silk Filature, 83 Haichow Road,
residing at an unnumbered country house off Haichow Road.
    I have been employed together with Sung Ming Foo (沈明富)
and Pau Tung Kwong (包道光), residing at the same address, under
Woo Pau Jang (吳柏祥), sub-contractor, Mei Foong Silk Filature,
since July 1938 until 15th Feb. 1939 when the factory ceased work
for the Chinese New Year Festivities and has not re-opened since.
Prior to the factory closing a notice was posted by the owner
to the effect that wages would be paid on 25th Feb. 1939.
I visited my mother-in-law, named Koo Kyung Doo (顧金大)
residing 17 Toh Sing Li, Rue Du Marche, and stayed there until
the 26/2/39 on which date I returned to the factory for my
salary but Woo Pau Jang refused to pay same unless I handed
over my pass to him, this I refused to do stating that my pass
had been obtained by the proprietor of the factory. After
making this statement Woo Pau Jang again refused to pay the
wages due to me following which an argument ensued which
subsequently led to blows being struck. On the termination of the
fight which was witnessed by many other employees of the Mei
Fong Silk Filature, Woo Pau Jang stated that as a result of
the fight he had "lost face" and would therefore call several
loafers to assault and cause me bodily injury. At about 4.00 p.m.
28/2/39 a friend of mine named Pang Miau Yi (彭妙儀) informed
me that there was a crowd of loafers coming to assault me towards
(28/2/39) at the instigation of Woo Pau Jang. On receipt of this

顾沛之（Koo Pai Nyiu，注：后文签名为 Koo Pai Diu，正文为 Koo Pai Nyui/Nyiu，中文名对应顾沛元/顾沛之，此处依标题译为顾沛之，但结合前文 Koo Pai Hyiu/Kyiu，应为同一人，即顾沛元。标题写的是 Koo Pai Nyiu (顧沛之)，但前文是 Koo Pai Hyiu (顾沛元)。这可能是档案记录的不一致。我将严格遵循每段的原文注释。此处标题明确写了中文“顧沛之”，故译为顾沛之。但需注意与前文“顾沛元”可能是同一人的不同记录。）
苏州                                D. S. Craig
杨树浦巡捕房        1939年2月28日                     职员 郑振儒 (Chin Cheng Ju).

我叫顾沛之（Koo Pai Nyui），30岁，苏州人，男性：
受雇于海州路83号美豐丝厂，
居住在海州路旁一处无门牌号的乡间房屋。
    自1938年7月至1939年2月15日，我与沈明富（Sung Ming Foo）和包道光（Pau Tung Kwong，注：前文为 Pao Sung Kuang 包松光，此处名字略有不同，依原文译）同住一处，在美豐丝厂分包商吴柏祥（Woo Pau Jang）手下工作。1939年2月15日工厂因春节庆典停工，此后一直未重新开工。在工厂关闭前，厂主张贴告示，称工资将于1939年2月25日发放。
    我去探望了住在市场路（Rue Du Marche）德兴里17号的岳母顾金大（Koo Kyung Doo），并在那里住到1939年2月26日。当天我回工厂领取薪水，但吴柏祥拒绝支付，除非我将通行证交给他。我拒绝了，声明我的通行证是由厂主办理的。在我做出这一声明后，吴柏祥再次拒绝支付欠我的工资，随后发生了争吵，进而演变为肢体冲突。在许多其他美豐丝厂员工的目睹下，斗殴结束后，吴柏祥声称因为这次斗殴他“丢了面子”，因此将叫几个流氓来殴打我，使我身体受伤。1939年2月28日下午4点左右，我的朋友彭妙儀（Pang Miau Yi）通知我，有一群流氓正朝我这边过来，意图在吴柏祥的唆使下殴打我。收到此消息后，我去朋友彭妙儀家中躲藏，

page_data.en:
2.

to avoid being assaulted. At 5.30 p.m. 28/2/39, a Chinese
detective located me at the home of my friend named Bang Miau
Yi, situated at 16 Linching Faung Linching Road where on being
questioned I stated the aforegoing facts as the cause of the
trouble.
This is my true statement.

Signed by Koo Pai Diu.

以避免被殴打。1939年2月28日下午5时30分，一名华籍侦探在我朋友彭妙儀（Bang Miau Yi，注：前文 Pang，此处 Bang，音同）位于临青路（Linching Road）16号林清坊（Linching Faung，音译）的家中找到了我。在接受讯问时，我陈述了上述引发骚乱的事实。

Sang Ming Foo [中文签名]
Taushing                                        D. S. Craig.
Y'poo Stn.          28/2/39                     Clerk Chin Cheng Ju.

    My name is Sang Ming Foo, age 34, Taushing, S/coolie,
employed and residing at the Mei Foong Silk Filature, 83 Haicho
Road.
    I have been employed at the Mei Foong Silk Filature,
together with Koo Pai Kyiu and Pau Sung Kwang under Woo Pau
Jang, sub-contractor at the above factory.
    On the 15/2/39 the factory ceased work for the Chinese
New Year Festivities but a notice was posted by the owner to
the effect that wages would be paid on the 24/2/39. For 13 days
work, viz. 2/2/39 to 15/2/39 I was entitled to $19.80 wages but
I only received $15.00 from Woo Pau Jang, the remaining $4.80
being deducted by Woo Pau Jang as pass fee, this fee would
allow me to keep the pass in my possession. I remonstrated with
Woo Pau Jang informing him that I had received my pass from the
Japanese pass through the proprietor of the factory, and not
through him, therefore, it was no concern of his whether I was
in possession of a pass or otherwise. I did not report the
extortion to the proprietor as I have not seen him since the
factory ceased work on the 15/2/39. At about 7 p.m. on the
26/2/39 at the factory workers quarters I witnessed a quarrel
between Woo Pau Jang and Koo Pai Kyiu which led to blows being
struck by both because the latter had refused to pay $5.00
extortion as a fee to retain possession of his Japanese pass
issued in the name of the proprietor of the factory.
    Following the fight Woo Pau Jang ran away and I have
not seen since. On the 28/2/39 I returned from Shanghai at
6.30 p.m. and did not see any leafers come to the factory.
This is my true statement.
                                            Signed: Sang Ming Foo.

桑明福 [中文签名]
陶辛                                        D. S. Craig.
杨树浦巡捕房          1939年2月28日                     书记员陈成祖。

    我叫桑明福，34岁，陶辛人，苦力，
受雇并居住在海州路83号美丰缫丝厂。
    我与顾柏秋和鲍松光一同受雇于上述工厂的分包商吴宝章手下，在美丰缫丝厂工作。
    1939年2月15日，工厂因中国新年庆祝活动停工，但厂主张贴告示，称工资将于1939年2月24日发放。对于13天的工作，即1939年2月2日至1939年2月15日，我应得工资19.80元，但我仅从吴宝章处收到15.00元，剩余的4.80元被吴宝章作为通行证费用扣除，此费用允许我保留通行证在我手中。我向吴宝章提出抗议，告知他我的通行证是通过厂主从日本人那里获得的，而不是通过他，因此我是否持有通行证与他无关。由于自1939年2月15日工厂停工后我就未见过厂主，所以我没有向厂主报告这起勒索事件。1939年2月26日晚上7点左右，在工厂工人宿舍，我目睹了吴宝章与顾柏秋之间的争吵，双方进而动手互殴，原因是后者拒绝支付5.00元的勒索费以保留以其厂主名义签发的日本通行证的持有权。
    斗殴发生后，吴宝章逃跑了，此后我再未见过他。1939年2月28日下午6点30分我从上海回来，没有看到任何流浪汉来到工厂。这是我的真实陈述。
                                            签名：桑明福。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Sung Keng Fah (沈根发)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S. Brotherton
at Y'poo Stn. on the 28-2-39 and interpreted by Clerk Chiu Chang Ju.

My name is Sung Keng Fah, 33, Shanghai, resident at my
employers address. I am a chauffeur- driving licence F.M.C.
No. 15769- employed by the Ford Hire Service, Avenue Edward VII.
Driving Hire-car F.M.C. Licence No. 12337.

I was in company with the last witness, Vai Ma Long (施米郎)
driving hire-car F.M.C. Licence No. 12337 at the said time, date
and places stated by him. I hereby, corroborate his statement
to the best of my belief.

As I was following witnesses' hire-car the whole time, the
only instructions I received from the five occupants of my car,
was to follow the car in front, namely the previous witnesses'.
The occupants reason for driving along the various Roads
in the Yulin and Yangtsepoo Districts is not apparent to me.
However, should I be again confronted by any one of the occupant
I think I could identify one or more of them.
Sung Keng Fah.

Having considered the fact, that this witnesses' statement
corresponds with that as is stated by the previous witness,
Vai Ma Long ( ), only a short statement, as is related
herein, was taken from him that neither might unnecessarily be

The witnesses employer's were informed of investigations

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下是沈根发（Sung Keng Fah）的陈述，他是上海人，由我 D.S. Brotherton 于1939年2月28日在杨树浦巡捕房录取，并由书记员邱昌菊翻译。

我叫沈根发，33岁，上海人，居住在雇主地址。我是司机——驾驶执照 F.M.C. 第15769号——受雇于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的福特租车行。驾驶租车牌照号为 F.M.C. 第12337号。

当时，我与上一位证人施米郎（Vai Ma Long）在一起，驾驶着他说的那辆牌照号为 F.M.C. 第12337号的租车，时间、日期和地点均如他所述。在此，我尽我所知证实他的陈述。

由于我全程跟随证人的租车，我从车上的五名乘客那里收到的唯一指令就是跟随前面的车，即前一位证人的车。我不清楚乘客们驾车穿行榆林和杨浦区各条道路的原因。然而，如果再次面对任何一名乘客，我想我能认出其中一人或多人。
沈根发。

鉴于该证人的陈述与前一位证人施米郎（ ）的陈述相符，考虑到这一点，仅从他那里获取了如上所述的简短陈述，以免不必要地拘留他们，而是让他们尽快离开。

Vai Bu Long (□ □ □)
Haimen                                D. S. Bretherton
Y'poo Stn.          28/2/39                  Clerk Chin Cheng Ju.

My name is Vai Bu Long, age 37, native of Haimen, resident
at No.11 Wong Ka Toon (□ □ □) off Great Western Road. I am
employed by the Ford Hire Service, Ave. Edward VII., as a
chauffeur F.M.C. driving licence No.8659 and drive hire-car F.M.
C. Lic. No.12374. At 3.57 p.m. on the 28/2/39 I was instructed
together with another chauffeur driving hire-car F.M.C. Lic. No.
12337 to drive from the Avenue Edward VII Service Station
(to which station we had both just returned) to No.35, Lane 134 Thorburn
Road and there pick up a fare. Arriving at about 4.10 p.m. both
our cars were met by ten male Chinese, who were standing on the
pavement outside the entrance the aforementioned address.
They were well dressed in Chinese long gowns and overcoats with
an appearance known to be that of the loafer element. They
then split up into two parties, five in each and boarded our
cars. One of the male's who boarded my car had a bundle (size
about 12" x 8") in his possession wrapped in a length of black
cloth, contents of which I do not know. Then, speaking in
Shanghai dialect with a Kompo accent, one of the male's
instructed me to drive along various roads indicating no
particular destination. The Roads traversed are as follows:-
North along Thorburn Road turning east into Yulin; north into
Chemulpo turning east into Baikal thence in continuation east
along Hockien turning south into Ningwu stopping at the corner
of Ningwu and Haichow Roads.
Coming to a standstill three of the males alighted only
to be joined by four more from the hire-car at my rear- there
were many persons of the mill workers type about at the time-
page_data.zh:
魏布龙（□ □ □）
海门                                D. S. Bretherton
杨树浦巡捕房          1939年2月28日                  书记员陈成祖。

我叫魏布龙，37岁，海门人，居住在大西路旁王家屯（□ □ □）11号。我受雇于爱多亚路（Ave. Edward VII）的福特租车行，担任司机，F.M.C. 驾驶执照第8659号，驾驶租车牌照号为 F.M.C. 第12374号。1939年2月28日下午3点57分，我接到指令，与另一位驾驶牌照号为 F.M.C. 第12337号租车的司机一起，从爱多亚路服务站（我们两人刚回到该站）驱车前往索伯恩路（Thorburn Road）134弄35号去接一位乘客。大约下午4点10分到达时，我们的两辆车被十名中国男子拦住，他们站在上述地址入口外的人行道上。他们穿着考究的中式长衫和大衣，外表看起来像是众所周知的游手好闲之徒。随后他们分成两组，每组五人，登上了我们的车。登上我车的一名男子手中拿着一个包裹（大小约12英寸 x 8英寸），用一块黑布包裹着，我不知道里面是什么。然后，其中一名男子用带有江北口音的上海话指令我沿着各种道路行驶，没有指明具体目的地。经过的道路如下：沿索伯恩路向北，向东转入榆林路；向北进入齐木浦路（Chemulpo），向东转入贝加尔路（Baikal），然后继续向东沿福建路（Hockien）行驶，向南转入宁武路，停在宁武路与海州路的拐角处。
停车后，三名男子下车，随即又有四人从我后面的租车上下来加入他们——当时周围有许多类似工厂工人的类型的人——

page_data.en:
2.

they left the car but I did not observe in what direction they
went being absent from the car but three or four minutes when
they boarded my car instructed me to drive to Y'poo Road and
thence to Linching turning west into Hochien, thence along
Hochien into Baikal; Chemulpo; thence along Pingliang Road.
On nearing the Pingliang Road market the time would be about
4.55 p.m., I was instructed to stop, where all occupants of the
two cars alighted, one of the male's telling me to wait. As the
males were about to saunter towards the market proper, I saw
them suddenly run off, without paying their fare, in all
directions, likewise, did the occupants of the other hire-car.
Looking about I saw a foreign detective approaching accompanied
by a Chinese detective.
I think, if confronted by one or more of the occupants
again, I could identify them.
It is well to mention, that during the time the occupants
travelled in my hire-car I did not overhear anything untoward,
likely to be of any assistance to the Police.

（签名）
L 3 39
Val Bi Long.
page_data.zh:
2.

他们离开了车子，但我没有观察到他们朝哪个方向走去，因为我离开车子只有三四分钟，当他们重新登上我的车时，指令我开往杨树浦路，然后到临青路，向西转入霍钦路（Hochien），然后沿霍钦路进入贝加尔路；齐木浦路；然后沿平凉路行驶。
接近平凉路市场时，时间大约是下午4点55分，我接到指令停车，两辆车的所有乘客都下了车，其中一名男子告诉我等待。当这些男子正要闲逛走向市场内部时，我看到他们突然向四面八方跑开，没有付车费，另一辆租车的乘客也是如此。环顾四周，我看到一名外国侦探在一名称中国侦探的陪同下走近。
我想，如果再次面对其中一名或多名乘客，我能认出他们。
值得一提的是，在乘客乘坐我的租车期间，我没有偷听到任何可能对警方有帮助的不寻常事情。

（签名）
1939年3月
Val Bi Long.

Duck Slaughterers - Unrest
Unrest now exists among some 100 employees of various local duck slaughter-houses who are agitating against a decision of their employers to pay their wages yearly instead of monthly with effect from February 1934. They are also dissatisfied with the failure of their employers to observe the agreement relating to their treatment. It is learned that these slaughterers will resort to a strike should their employers ignore their opposition.

World Bookstore - Dismissed workers meet to discuss formation of hunger strike groups
Seven ex-workers of the World Bookstore, 3-5 Dalny Road, held a meeting in the office of the "World Bookstore Dismissed Workers' Appeal Committee" in the Zung Hsiang Koh Temple, New North Gate, at 4 p.m. January 17. It was decided to report to the local Kuomintang that, as their demand for reinstatement could not be entertained, the dismissed workers would organise hunger strike groups and appeal to the Bureau of Social Affairs.

January 16, 1934. Afternoon Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:
DISPUTE AT THE MEI FOONG SILK WEAVING WORKS.
At a meeting called yesterday afternoon by the Social Bureau regarding the dispute at the Mei Foong Silk Weaving Works on Haichow Road, the following measures were passed:-
1. That the management suspend operations till the end of February.
2. That the management grant a loan of $10 to each operative for the period of suspension of work, the loan to be refunded in two instalments when work is resumed.
3. That the workers be allowed to reside in the Works quarters but the number be limited.
4. That should the management be unable to re-open the Works at the date suggested, the hands be discharged.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:
DISPUTE AT THE DAH CHUNG HWA VULCANIZING WORKS.
In November last year, the Dah Chung Hwa Vulcanizing Works on Route Zikawei dismissed nine workers who were prominent members of the Union.
Acting on instructions from the local Tangpu and other political organs, the dismissed workers attempted to resume, but were refused admittance by the management.
A petition will be submitted to-day to the Social Bureau.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:
B.A.T. WORKERS RESUME.
With reference to the dispute at the Tin Foil Department of the British-American Tobacco Old Factory at Pootung, the workers resumed work at 7 a.m. yesterday. An official of the local Tangpu yesterday proceeded to Pootung and advised the operatives to await a settlement.

Mei Feng Silk Weaving Factory - dispute settled

Between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. January 15, the Bureau
of Social Affairs convened a meeting in its offices
at the New Civic Centre, with a view to settling the
dispute over the demand for retiring gratuities
by the workers of the Mei Feng Silk Weaving Factory,
17 Haichow Road. Representatives of both sides
concerned attended and it was decided that each of
the unemployed workers be paid a sum of $10.00 as re-
patriation fee which will be repayable on re-engagement
should the concern resume operation.

The Factory which employed a total of 314 hands
closed down at the end of December, 1933 (Vide I.R.
1-3/1/34).

S.N.R. & S.N.N.R. Woosung Works - meeting of workers

Between 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. January 15, one hundred
foremen of the Woosung Works held a meeting in their
workshop. Tsai Ching Foh (蔡金福), one of the delegates
who returned from Nanking, reported that as a result
of an appeal made to the Ministry of Railways, the latter
had promised to give a reply in connection with the
demand for the dismissal of the Chief of the Store
Department of the S.N.R. & S.N.N.R. within three days.
The meeting decided that should the Ministry of Railways
fail to settle the dispute in favour of the workers,
delegates be sent to Nanking to make further appeals.

Mei Feng Silk Weaving Factory - ex-workers agitate for
reopening of the concern

Some 300 ex-workers of the Mei Feng Silk Weaving
Factory ly Haichow Road, are agitating for the reopining
of the concern which in consequence of trade depression
closed down on December 31, 1933 (Vide I.R. 1-3/1/34).
During the afternoon of January 1, some 120 ex-employees
held a meeting on the premises of the factory, when it was
decided that four delegates be assigned to negotiate with
the management regarding resumption of operations. It was
also resolved that all affected workers should contribute
$3.00 each to cover expenses incurred by the delegates.
It is learned that the ex-workers propose to hold a meeting
this morning, January 4, on the premises of the concern to
discuss ways and means of soliciting assistance from the
Chinese Authorities.

On receipt of this letter uniform police and detectives were posted in the mill to take precautionary measures.

At 1.25 p.m. (31/12/33) a telephone message was received from the management to the effect that workers were creating trouble in the machine room.

A party of police with C/Inspector Foley, Inspector West and S.I. Craik immediately proceeded to the filature where numerous employees were found in the compound abusing the owner, Nee Dah Tsun.
